facts: Kiefer and Renshaw reported that molybdenum-bearing types 316 and 317 were the most resistant to sulfuric acid at low temperatures.
NBS Circular 592 states that at about 150°F all of the stainless steels corrode in practically all concentrations of sulfuric acid from [UNREADABLE lower bound] to 95 percent.
Roach and Hall reported that molybdenum-bearing stainless steels were useful at room temperature in sulfuric acid concentrations below 15 percent and above 85 percent.
The Circular reports that resistance to sulfuric acid is improved in some cases by additions of copper or cerium.
NBS Circular 592 describes Hastelloy A as usefully resistant to sulfuric acid of all concentrations at temperatures up to about 160°F (presented as an example of a higher-resistance alloy).

Inference — For screening, do not conclude that stainless steel is acceptable for sulfuric-acid service at ≈150°F across concentrations; require alloy-, temperature-, and concentration-specific corrosion-rate data or select a more resistant alloy.
